title: Roadmap Conductor: commitment lanes for hosted endpoints and model health scoring
creator: Marta Singh
description:
Goal: define a repeatable quarterly cadence and commitment lanes for the Hosted API + Model Catalog that balances feature commitments, capacity hedges, and experimental lanes. This ticket centralizes the decision framework (commitment windows, rollback/backstop policies, and model-health scoring) that PMs, Eng, and DX can use when drafting sprint commitments for the quarter.

Background: multiple teams have requested clearer guardrails for what constitutes a 'commit' vs an 'experiment' for hosted endpoints. Without explicit lanes we overcommit capacity, cause surprise model rotations, and struggle to correlate OKR signals with operational metrics (latency, cost/unit, model regressions). This initiative pulls together: commitment lanes (Commit / Hedge / Experiment), a lightweight model health scorecard, and a coordination playbook for canaries and staged rollouts.

Deliverables:
- Commitment lanes rubric and calendar (commit windows, buffer policy, deprecation notice windows)
- Model health scoring template (quality + reliability + cost signals) and how it maps to lane eligibility
- Runbook for scheduling canaries, backfill capacity, and automatic fallback triggers
- Example quarter plan for a 3-model hosted endpoint bundle with contingency lanes and staff allocation
- Stakeholder sign-off checklist (Eng, SRE, Legal for data policies if applicable)

Success criteria (high level):
- All Hosted API model additions/rotations in Q2 must be categorized under a lane with an accepted scorecard
- >90% of scheduled canaries have predefined rollback/metrics windows in Console dashboards
- Product/Eng satisfaction score on runway predictability improves by 30% in post-cycle retrospective
acceptance_criteria: Written commitment-lane rubric accepted by Eng/PM/Design
Model health scorecard template uploaded to Confluence and linked from PRD
Playbook for canary scheduling and rollback published in the Console ops runbook
One example hosted endpoint plan mapped into the quarterly calendar with contingency lanes
